source_metadata.title: Weight Loss-Dependent Changes in Body Composition and Bone Health in People With Obesity and Type 1 Diabetes Treated With Liraglutide, Semaglutide, or Tirzepatide

source_consistency_findings.details: For the 5%-10% weight-loss stratum, Table 3 reports fat-mass change -5.41% with 95% CI -14.79 to +3.97 and p=0.019, whereas the Results narrative on page 3 reports 95% CI -14.79 to -3.97 with the same p=0.019. The atom anchored to Table 3 preserves the table value; the discrepancy is not silently repaired.

The Results narrative describes weight-loss correlations using R² values (lean mass R²=0.38; fat mass R²=0.68), whereas Figure 1 labels the corresponding Spearman statistics as R=0.38 and R=0.68. Figure-anchored atoms preserve the Figure 1 R labels.

The abstract reports total lean-mass loss associated with body-weight loss as R²=0.36 (p<0.001), while Figure 1 shows Spearman R=0.38 (p=0.0013) for lean-mass loss. Both source locations are retained as an internal reporting discrepancy rather than reconciled by inference.

extraction_limitations: No supplementary source material was specified or used.
The article pools liraglutide, semaglutide, and tirzepatide for the principal body-composition analyses; drug-specific comparative effects are therefore not extracted as comparative efficacy claims.
Table 3 contains an internally inconsistent confidence interval for fat-mass change in the 5%-10% weight-loss stratum; the table value was preserved in the atom and the discrepancy is flagged above.
Safety ascertainment was limited in the source to severe hypoglycaemia and diabetic ketoacidosis; absence of other adverse events cannot be inferred.
